Weighted displacement quotient: did crime move next door?

Source: R/wdqx.R
wdqx.Rd

Asks whether an intervention in an area pushed crime into the area around it (displacement) or reduced it there too (a diffusion of benefits). Counts before and after the intervention are needed for the treated area a, a buffer b around it and a control area c that neither can reach (see bufas() for drawing them). With subscripts 0 before and 1 after, the measures of Bowers and Johnson (2003), as Guerette (2009, Appendix B, equations 1 to 4) states them:

Usage

wdqx(a, b, c)

Arguments

a, b, c

The counts before and after in the treated area, the buffer and the control: two numbers from 0 each, before first; those of c positive.

Value

A named numeric vector: sm, bdm, wdq, ge, ne, ea, eb and tne.

Details

  • the success measure sm = a1 / c1 - a0 / c0, the change in the treated area relative to the control; negative when the intervention worked;

  • the buffer displacement measure bdm = b1 / c1 - b0 / c0; positive when crime rose in the buffer (displacement), negative when it fell (diffusion);

  • the weighted displacement quotient wdq = bdm / sm. With sm negative, wdq above 0 is a diffusion of benefits, below 0 displacement, and below -1 displacement larger than the gain in the treated area;

  • the gross effect ge = a0 - a1, the fall in the treated area, and the net effect ne = a0 / c0 - a1 / c1 (that is -sm), the fall relative to the control;

  • the total net effect tne = (a0 c1 / c0 - a1) + (b0 c1 / c0 - b1), the crimes prevented in the treated area and the buffer together (positive when crime was prevented), with ea = a0 c1 / c0 and eb = b0 c1 / c0 the counts expected after had both areas followed the control. ge and tne count crimes, so they need counts, not rates.

The quotient means little when sm is close to 0 (NA at exactly 0) or the counts are small; the control must be like the other two areas in trend, and far enough not to be reached by either. Guerette's worked example (Appendix D: the treated area 207 before and 110 after, the buffer 178 and 157, the control 308 and 318) gives ge 97, ne 0.326 and tne 130.5, as printed there; the guide prints the quotient as 0.411, which its own formula and counts do not give (they give 0.258).

References

Bowers, K. J. and Johnson, S. D. (2003). Measuring the geographical displacement and diffusion of benefit effects of crime prevention activity. Journal of Quantitative Criminology, 19(3), 275-301. doi:10.1023/A:1024909009240

Guerette, R. T. (2009). Analyzing Crime Displacement and Diffusion. Tool Guide No. 10. Center for Problem-Oriented Policing, Arizona State University.

Examples

# burglaries: treated 100 -> 60, buffer 50 -> 40, control 200 -> 180
wdqx(a = c(100, 60), b = c(50, 40), c = c(200, 180))
#>          sm         bdm         wdq          ge          ne          ea 
#> -0.16666667 -0.02777778  0.16666667 40.00000000  0.16666667 90.00000000 
#>          eb         tne 
#> 45.00000000 35.00000000 
# Guerette (2009), Appendix D
wdqx(a = c(207, 110), b = c(178, 157), c = c(308, 318))
#>           sm          bdm          wdq           ge           ne           ea 
#>  -0.32616597  -0.08421139   0.25818569  97.00000000   0.32616597 213.72077922 
#>           eb          tne 
#> 183.77922078 130.50000000
